subject.title: Feature: Webchat / Control UI inline button support (buttons parameter, callback RPC, capabilities config)

question: Should WebChat inline buttons use the shared presentation typed-action contract with an authenticated same-session chat.callback RPC, and should webhook callback routing be deferred from v1?
rationale: The requested work crosses public Gateway protocol, browser UI rendering, config/capability shape, and callback security semantics; source inspection shows the gap is real, but automation cannot choose the permanent public contract or webhook boundary.

options.title: Use typed presentation plus RPC
options.body: Adopt shared presentation button/select blocks, add final-only WebChat projection, and route clicks through an authenticated chat.callback method before considering webhooks.

options.title: Require legacy buttons compatibility
options.body: Ask contributors to preserve a buttons-shaped compatibility layer, accepting extra API surface and migration risk for closer Telegram parity.

options.title: Defer WebChat buttons
options.body: Leave WebChat text-only for now and keep the issue open until a broader browser interaction roadmap is approved.

recommendation.title: Use typed presentation plus RPC
recommendation.body: Adopt shared presentation button/select blocks, add final-only WebChat projection, and route clicks through an authenticated chat.callback method before considering webhooks.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest available routing candidate from issue timeline mentions and recent current-main Gateway/WebChat-adjacent work, while the remaining question is product/security direction.
